mt_udl_left_middle.blurb: UDL Left/Middle is one of the busier sectors at Point of Rocks, in the northwest corner of Montana between Whitefish and Eureka. Eleven routes make up the wall, nine of them bolted and two traditional, covering an easy-to-hard spread from about 5.6 up through the low 5.12 range, with the largest cluster around 5.9 and 5.10. The rock is argillite, and the wall stays shaded for most of the day, which makes it a handy pick when the valley is hot. The walk in is short: an old logging road, then a side path into the trees leads to the Middle section, and the Left section lies a little farther along the cliff base. A good fit for mixed-ability groups.

mt_boundary_crag.blurb: Boundary Crag is a small limestone sport wall in the Allenspur area of Paradise Valley, a short drive south of Livingston. It holds eleven bolted routes and is the first big face you meet on the trail up. The grades skew toward the middle and upper end: a single route near 5.7, one at 5.9, four in the 5.10 range and five at 5.11, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on steeper, more sustained lines rather than beginners. The valley setting gives wide views, and wind can be a factor, so a layer is worth carrying. Allenspur as a whole is usually best in spring and fall.

mt_carpenter_boulder.blurb: Carpenter Boulder is a single house-sized block tucked among trees on the west side of Gallatin Canyon, part of the Cascade Creek bouldering zone south of Bozeman. The gneiss block carries eleven problems that run from an easy warm-up to some very hard lines, with a spread through the V3 to V5 range and a few testing problems above V6. Expect a mix of tall slabs and more technical moves on the back side. The zone sits high, in a talus field reached by a long uphill walk, so it is a summer and early-fall destination that tends to be quiet compared with the roadside crags.

mt_atrium_the.blurb: The Atrium is the nearer of the two bouldering zones at Wolf Butte, a shallow limestone canyon east of Great Falls on the High Plains. It holds eleven problems on the lower end of the scale: mostly easy to moderate, topping out around V4, with a handful of beginner lines. That makes it the usual place to start, with warm-ups before you move up canyon to the Graveyard. The limestone there is newer and can feel sharp and rough on skin, though it is grippy. The canyon offers both sun and shade but can get hot in summer, so spring is a pleasant time to visit.

mt_tick_farm.blurb: Tick Farm is a wall of eleven bolted routes on the north rim of Mill Creek, in the Bitterroot country south of Missoula, and it is the busiest sector at the top of the approach gully. Climbs range from about 5.8 to 5.11, with most sitting in the 5.10 range, so it favors solid intermediates. The routes are named with tick puns, which is fair warning: the canyon is known for the insects in season. Getting there takes a steady uphill hike of roughly half an hour to an hour from the trailhead, and the rim picks up winter sun, so it can be climbed through much of the year. Wear a helmet, since big walls above shed rock.
